boundary.in_scope: The taxonomy of financial securities and their defining attributes: equity/stock (common stock, preferred stock, depositary receipts); debt/bonds (government, corporate and municipal bonds, money-market instruments such as treasury bills, commercial paper and certificates of deposit, and structured/asset-backed and mortgage-backed debt); derivatives (options including calls and puts, futures, forwards, swaps including interest-rate, currency and credit-default swaps, and warrants); and pooled funds (mutual funds, exchange-traded funds, hedge funds, money-market funds and closed-end funds), together with their issuers (governments, corporations, municipalities and supranational entities) and underlying assets (commodities, currencies, market indices, interest rates and real estate). The instruments' defining attributes are in scope (issuer, maturity, coupon, dividend, face value, strike price, notional amount and net asset value), as are the relations among them (issuedBy/hasIssuer, hasUnderlying, paysCoupon, hasMaturity, convertibleInto, tracksIndex).
boundary.out_of_scope: Trading mechanics, order types and market microstructure; specific companies, tickers or other real-world instances of instruments; accounting and tax treatment beyond plain definitions; valuation/pricing models and risk analytics; and regulatory filing or issuance procedures. These are excluded so that the corpus scope equals the gold-standard TBox, which covers only the taxonomy of securities, their issuers, underlying assets and defining attributes, and explicitly excludes trading mechanics, accounting/tax treatment and real instances.
